---
title: Generated code
description: Detect generated files and generated symbols the way the analyzer driver does.
---

Roslyn recognizes generated code in two independent ways, and the package exposes both.

## Generated files

`SyntaxTree.IsGeneratedCode` looks at the file. In order, it uses:

1. the `generated_code` option of `.editorconfig`, when it is set;
2. the well-known file names: `.g.cs`, `.g.i.cs`, `.designer.cs`, `.generated.cs` and `TemporaryGeneratedFile_*`;
3. an `<auto-generated>` comment at the start of the file.

Pass the `AnalyzerOptions` of an analysis context, or the `AnalyzerConfigOptionsProvider` of a source generator, to read
the `.editorconfig` option: the overload that only takes a `CancellationToken` applies the last two rules.
`GeneratedCodeExtensions.IsGeneratedCodeFile(path)` applies the file name rule alone.

## Generated symbols

`ISymbol.IsGeneratedCodeSymbol` looks at the symbol: it walks the symbol and the symbols that contain it, up to the
assembly, looking for `[System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCode]`. A symbol declared in several files, such as a partial
type, is never generated code, and the walk stops there:

<!-- ref:../../tests/Meziantou.Framework.Roslyn.Tests/RoslynHelperTests.cs;region=Roslyn_IsGeneratedCodeSymbol;format=md-fenced-code-block;dedent=true -->
```csharp
var compilation = CSharpCompilation.Create(
    "Sample",
    [CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText("""
        [System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCode("Tool", "1.0")]
        public class Generated
        {
            public void Method() { }
        }

        public class Handwritten { }
        """)],
    [MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(typeof(object).Assembly.Location)]);

// Resolve the attribute once, then test the symbols
var generatedCodeAttribute = compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCodeAttribute");
var symbol = compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("Generated")!.GetMembers("Method").Single();
Assert.True(symbol.IsGeneratedCodeSymbol(generatedCodeAttribute));
Assert.False(compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName("Handwritten")!.IsGeneratedCodeSymbol(generatedCodeAttribute));
```
<!-- endref -->

Resolve the attribute type once per compilation and pass it, rather than the `Compilation` overload, when you test many
symbols.

## Match the analyzer driver

With `GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.None`, the analyzer driver skips a location when either check matches, for symbol,
syntax and operation actions alike. The symbol check covers the declaration of the symbol that carries the attribute:
another type of the same file without the attribute is still analyzed. Use both checks to make the same decision in
your own code, for instance in a [diagnostic filter](06-ReportingDiagnostics.md#filter-diagnostics).

A source generator gets no special treatment: Roslyn does not flag the trees it adds to the compilation. When the hint
name of a generated file has no well-known suffix, its content has no `<auto-generated>` comment and its types have no
`[GeneratedCode]` attribute, every analyzer runs on it, including those that opted out of generated code. Name the
generated files `*.g.cs`, or start them with `// <auto-generated/>`.
